KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and seasonable through mid-week. Some frost
is likely in spots tonight.

Weak high pressure over the Gulf Coast states will build east 
through tonight and then move offshore on Wednesday. Generally 
tranquil conditions will persist through Wednesday though it 
will continue to be a bit breezy this afternoon. This is due to 
a pressure gradient between the high to our south and another 
low passing by to our north. Generally expect west winds around 
10 to 15 gusting upwards of 20 to 25 mph this afternoon before 
diminishing after sunset. 

The pressure gradient will weaken tonight helping lead to lighter 
winds that could even been near calm by later tonight over the more 
sheltered locations. Mainly clear skies will also help lead to 
good radiational cooling despite the airmass not being all that
cold. Generally expect lows ranging from the mid 30 to the low 
to mid 40s. This will likely lead to some patchy frost overnight
and we've issued a Frost Advisory for portions of southern NJ 
where the growing season is active. The Advisory runs from 1 AM 
to 9 AM Wednesday and is for Salem, Cumberland, Gloucester, and 
Camden Counties. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...A  strengthening storm system organizes off the
northern Mid-Atlantic coast Thursday into Friday.

A vigorous upper-level trough continues to be forecast to 
evolve across the eastern U.S. later this week and into the 
weekend. This supports a surface low that strengthens as it tracks 
across portions of the Mid-Atlantic and then especially just 
offshore of the Northeast. It appears that low pressure will tend to 
consolidate off the New Jersey coast on Thursday, then deepen as it 
tracks north-northeast toward the Canadian Maritimes Friday into 
Saturday. While there are still some differences with the handling 
of the embedded short waves, there is better model clustering with 
the surface low placement/track. Overall, it will be unsettled 
across our region as we go through Thursday and Friday.

The strength of the parent upper-level trough results in a 
colder air mass moving in with time, however the initial air 
mass is not all that cold (the lack of a cold antecedent air mass). 
As the surface low consolidates off the northern Mid-Atlantic coast, 
the winds will turn more out of the northwest and this will increase 
the cold air advection. This will result in some colder air seeping 
southeastward later Thursday night but especially Friday into Friday 
night. The air mass may become sufficiently cold enough mostly 
across our far northwestern zones for a rain/snow mix or even some 
snow across the higher elevations, confined particularly to the 
southern Poconos. Otherwise, a rain event is forecast. The amount of 
precipitation (rain and/or snow) will depend on the ultimate track 
of the surface low and whether a deformation zones wraps back into 
our northern to central areas. 

The model consensus looks to be more of a northward positioning
of the surface low, which if this ends up occurring would result
in less rainfall with a southward extent across our area. The 
coastal impacts, including the potential for stronger onshore 
winds and also (minor) tidal flooding, are a little less certain
because the surface low track right over our area would lessen 
the residence time of the (stronger) onshore flow. Prior to the 
low fully consolidating offshore, some elevated instability could
get into especially portions of our coastal plain and therefore
a rumble of thunder is possible later Thursday night and Friday
morning. The strongest winds with this look to occur as the 
storm moves farther away and the cold air advection then increases
from the northwest. The main uncertainty is on how much precipitation
occurs with this event region-wide and the extent/amount of any
higher elevation snow (mainly for the southern Poconos). 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Much colder air Friday and over the weekend. 

In the wake of the storm, as it deepens and tracks toward the 
Canadian Maritimes over the weekend, a colder air mass will be 
in place across our area. In addition, a tightened pressure gradient 
coupled with deeper mixing will result in a period of breezy to 
windy conditions over the weekend. The strongest winds look to occur 
on Saturday, with peak gusts to about 35 mph, then while still gusty 
on Sunday it appears the speeds come down a little. Daytime 
temperatures on Friday and Saturday should not get out of the 40s 
for many areas, with temperatures at night dropping into the 20s to 
low 30s. Where the growing season is still active across Delmarva, 
parts of southern New Jersey and far southeastern Pennsylvania. 
There could even be some lake effect snow and/or rain showers into 
the southern Poconos on Saturday. 

Temperatures start to moderate a bit on Sunday and then some more on 
Monday. Despite that, high temperatures are only in the upper 40s to 
low 50s each day which is still below average for this time of year.
